definitions.explanation: Persimmons that have been peeled and air-dried until they shrivel and develop a sweet, chewy texture coated with a natural white frost of sugars. A traditional Japanese preserved food and seasonal winter treat.

examples.japanese: {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎年|まいとし}→毎年：00731_maitoshi⟧{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother makes dried persimmons every year.

examples.japanese: ⟦{軒先|のきさき}→軒先：08402_nokisaki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{柿|かき}→柿：04384_kaki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{吊|つる}されて、{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{待|ま}っている→待つ：00469_matsu⟧。
examples.english: Persimmons hang under the eaves, waiting to become dried persimmons.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{干|ほ}す→干す：00115_hosu⟧ (to dry) + ⟦{柿|かき}→柿：04384_kaki⟧ (persimmon), with the kaki reading shifting to gaki through rendaku.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make dried persimmons
- {干|ほ}し{柿|がき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{吊|つる}す: to hang persimmons to dry
- ⟦{甘|あま}い→甘い：00617_amai⟧{干|ほ}し{柿|がき}: sweet dried persimmon

CULTURAL NOTE:
A classic autumn-to-winter food. Peeled astringent persimmons are hung from strings under eaves; over weeks they lose moisture, the tannins break down, and natural sugars crystallize on the surface as a white bloom. Often given as gifts and used in osechi New Year cuisine.
